title: The Last Archive
subtitle: A Mystery Escape Room

room.name: The Reading Room of the Halloway Research Library
room.description: Dust hangs in the green glow of an emergency lamp. A heavy oak study desk sits beneath a tall bookshelf; an antique painting in a brass-locked frame hangs on the east wall. Built into the desk is a locked drawer with a four-dial combination lock. Beside the steel exit door, a digital security console blinks: LOCKDOWN ACTIVE - THREE SEALS REMAIN.

intro: You wake on the cold floor of an abandoned research library. A message flickers on the security console: 'Archive lockdown in progress. Authorised staff may release the door by restoring the three seals.' The archivist left a trail of clues before the building was sealed. Follow it - and get out before the lockdown becomes permanent.

desk.name: Study Desk
desk.description: A scarred oak desk. A green leather blotter covers its surface, and a torn note is pinned beneath a paperweight. Something glints between the stacked papers.
desk.examine_text: Under the paperweight you find a torn note in the archivist's handwriting: "The drawer remembers history - read the red spines from OLDEST to NEWEST." Pressed into the leather blotter is half of a symbol cipher: CRESCENT MOON = 5, STAR = 8. Between the papers lies a small ultraviolet lamp.

bookshelf.name: Bookshelf
bookshelf.description: Floor-to-ceiling shelves of grey archive volumes. Four books with red spines stand out from the rest.
bookshelf.examine_text: Each of the four red books carries a publication year and a single handwritten digit on its spine: 'Atlas of Tides' (1923) - 4; 'The Cartographer's Lament' (1887) - 2; 'Silent Engines' (1951) - 7; 'Ledger of Stars' (1902) - 9.

painting.name: Antique Painting
painting.description: An oil portrait of the library's founder, held in a heavy frame fixed to the wall by a small brass lock.
painting.examine_text: The frame is fixed to the wall by a small brass lock. Faint brush marks on the edge of the canvas suggest something was painted on the back.
painting.locked_text: The brass lock holds the frame firmly against the wall.
painting.unlocked_text: The brass key turns and the frame swings away from the wall. The back of the canvas looks blank - but the paint has a strange sheen, as if it was meant to be seen under different light.
painting.reveal_text: Under ultraviolet light, four symbols glow on the back of the canvas, each tagged with a Roman numeral: a TRIANGLE marked III, a CRESCENT MOON marked I, a CIRCLE marked IV and a STAR marked II.

drawer.name: Locked Drawer
drawer.description: A drawer built into the desk, secured by a four-dial combination lock.
drawer.examine_text: The drawer has four brass dials, each numbered 0 to 9. A tiny engraving reads: 'Ordered by history.'
drawer.opened_text: The dials click into place and the drawer slides open. Inside are a small brass key and a stiff card printed with symbols.

console.name: Security Console
console.description: A digital security console wired to the exit door. Its keypad accepts a four-digit override code.
console.examine_text: The screen reads: 'OVERRIDE REQUIRED. Enter the four-digit archive code. The code is written in the founder's constellation.'
console.opened_text: The console chimes: 'OVERRIDE ACCEPTED. Releasing staff keycard.' A slot opens and ejects a white exit keycard.

exit_door.name: Exit Door
exit_door.description: A heavy steel door held by an electromagnetic lock. A keycard reader glows red beside the handle.
exit_door.examine_text: The keycard reader glows red. A label reads: 'Staff keycard required. Keycards are issued by the security console.'

uv_lamp.name: UV Lamp
uv_lamp.description: A palm-sized ultraviolet lamp. Useful for revealing invisible ink.

brass_key.name: Brass Key
brass_key.description: A small brass key with a frame-maker's mark.

cipher_card.name: Cipher Card
cipher_card.description: The second half of the archivist's symbol cipher: TRIANGLE = 3, CIRCLE = 6, SQUARE = 1.

exit_keycard.name: Exit Keycard
exit_keycard.description: A white staff keycard issued by the security console.

clues.archivist_note: Torn note: read the red spines from OLDEST to NEWEST to open the drawer.
clues.red_spine_digits: Red spines: Atlas of Tides (1923) = 4, The Cartographer's Lament (1887) = 2, Silent Engines (1951) = 7, Ledger of Stars (1902) = 9.
clues.cipher_half_a: Desk blotter cipher: CRESCENT MOON = 5, STAR = 8.
clues.uv_symbols: Back of the painting (UV): TRIANGLE III, CRESCENT MOON I, CIRCLE IV, STAR II.
clues.constellation_order: The founder's constellation, in order: CRESCENT MOON, STAR, TRIANGLE, CIRCLE.

puzzle_1.name: Chronology of the Red Spines
puzzle_1.success_text: Ordered by publication year - 1887, 1902, 1923, 1951 - the digits read 2-9-4-7.
puzzle_1.hint: Every red spine has a year and a digit. The torn note on the desk tells you which order matters.

puzzle_2.name: The Hidden Constellation
puzzle_2.success_text: Read by their Roman numerals, the symbols form the founder's constellation: crescent moon, star, triangle, circle. Somewhere a relay clicks.
puzzle_2.hint: The Roman numerals beside the glowing symbols give their order. State the four symbols in that order.

puzzle_3.name: The Archivist's Cipher
puzzle_3.success_text: Moon 5, star 8, triangle 3, circle 6. The console accepts 5-8-3-6.
puzzle_3.hint: Translate the constellation symbol by symbol using both halves of the cipher - one half is on the desk blotter, the other on the card from the drawer.

escape_condition.text: You swipe the keycard. The reader turns green, the magnetic lock releases with a heavy clunk, and cold night air rushes in. You have escaped the Last Archive.
